newsitem.title: USA: Tosco could cut Unocal jobs -report.
newsitem.headline: Tosco could cut Unocal jobs -report.

text.p: Tosco Corp could cut up to 550 jobs after its completes the purchase of Unocal Corp's 76 Products Co this month and shifts its headquarters to Phoenix, according to a published report.
The Los Angeles Times quoted 76 Products Co President Lawrence Higby as saying some of the cuts would be voluntary.
A spokesman for the company declined to comment on the job cuts.
76 Products, now based in Costa Mesa, Calif., employs 3,600 people and holds $2.7 billion in assets in six western states, including 1,300 service stations.
Tosco agreed to buy 76 Products' refineries and other downstream assets from Unocal last November for about $1.4 billion.
Meanwhile, the union for Unocal refinery workers said last week disagreements over layoffs could prompt the union to strike at four Unocal refineries in California.
76 Products refines about 20 pct of California's gasoline, with the state's third-highest market share at 12.5 percent.
